recall_prompt: Say how you would resolve (2x² + 2x + 1)/(x³ + x²) into partial fractions — name each move in order.
insider_note: The first mark is the form: x² is the factor x repeated, so it needs a fraction over x AND one over x² — three fractions in all, and a form with only two cannot be made to match.

steps.label: Set up the form
steps.margin_note: First mark. x³ + x² = x²(x + 1). The x² is a repeated factor (x twice), so it gives A/x + B/x², and (x + 1) gives C/(x + 1).

recall.must_convey: That x³ + x² factorises as x²(x + 1) and the form is A/x + B/x² + C/(x + 1), with two fractions for the repeated factor x².
accept: take x squared common so the denominator is x squared into x plus one and write A over x plus B over x squared plus C over x plus one
x squared is a repeated factor so it gives A by x and B by x squared and x plus one gives C by x plus one
three fractions A by x, B by x square and C by x plus 1
x cube plus x square ni x square into x plus one ga rasi A by x plus B by x square plus C by x plus one ani pettali

heard_as: x squared into x plus one

steps.why: x² is the linear factor x repeated, exactly like (x − 1)², so it needs both 1/x and 1/x² denominators. The first move is always to factorise the denominator fully so every factor is seen.
common_mistakes: Writing A/x² + C/(x + 1) and missing the B/x fraction.
Treating x² as an irreducible quadratic and writing (Ax + B)/x².
Not taking x² common and writing a fraction over x³ + x².

steps.label: Clear the denominators
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Multiply by x²(x + 1). A keeps x(x + 1), B keeps (x + 1), C keeps x². Every term on the right is a polynomial.

recall.must_convey: That multiplying through gives 2x² + 2x + 1 = Ax(x + 1) + B(x + 1) + Cx².
accept: multiply both sides by x squared into x plus one to get two x squared plus two x plus one equals A x into x plus one plus B into x plus one plus C x squared
clear the denominators so A keeps x into x plus one, B keeps x plus one and C keeps x squared
multiply through by the whole denominator to get an identity in x
x square into x plus one tho multiply cheste A x into x plus one plus B into x plus one plus C x square vastundi
remove the fractions by multiplying with x squared times x plus one
heard_as: A x into x plus one

steps.why: After multiplying by x², the A/x term keeps one x and the B/x² term keeps none. Those leftover factors are what make x = 0 isolate B in the next step.
common_mistakes: Giving the A term x² instead of x(x + 1).
Giving the C term (x + 1) instead of x².

steps.label: Find the constants
steps.margin_note: Third mark. x = 0 gives B, x = −1 gives C, and A comes from the x² coefficient: A + C = 2. The repeated factor has one root, so one constant must come from a coefficient.

recall.must_convey: That x = 0 gives B = 1, x = −1 gives C = 1, and comparing x² coefficients gives A + C = 2, so A = 1.
accept: put x equals zero to get B equals one, x equals minus one to get C equals one, then compare x squared to get A plus C equals two so A is one
two substitutions give B one and C one and the x squared coefficient gives A one
A B and C are all one, B from x equals zero, C from x equals minus one and A from the coefficient of x squared
x equals zero pedithe B one, x equals minus one pedithe C one, x square coefficient compare cheste A one
the third constant comes from equating the x squared coefficients

steps.why: Substituting the roots 0 and −1 finds two constants directly. The x² coefficient on the right is A + C, because both Ax(x + 1) and Cx² contain x²; equating it to 2 finds A without any simultaneous equations.
common_mistakes: Reading the x² coefficient on the right as C only and forgetting Ax(x + 1) also gives Ax².
Putting x = −1 and getting 2(−1)² + 2(−1) + 1 as 5 instead of 1.
Trying a third substitution for A; no third root exists.

steps.label: Write the result
steps.margin_note: Last mark. All three constants are 1, so the answer is 1/x + 1/x² + 1/(x + 1). Write the original fraction on the left.

accept: the answer is one over x plus one over x squared plus one over x plus one

steps.why: The resolved form is the answer the examiner marks. Since every constant is 1, the final line is short, but it still has to show all three fractions.
common_mistakes: Writing the answer over x³ + x² again instead of as separate fractions.
Not checking: put x = 1 in the identity, 5 = 2 + 2 + 1. If the two sides differ, a constant is wrong.
